repair_summary: Two pieces of damage. (1) The env's stdlib threading.py was swapped for a wrapper that exec's /tmp/threading.py.original, which the Dockerfile then deleted, so `import threading` raises FileNotFoundError; the wrapper also added 15 ms sleeps to Lock/RLock. The original source is gone, but its compiled pyc (__pycache__/threading.cpython-310.pyc) survived. The repair takes the system /usr/lib/python3.10/threading.py (Ubuntu 3.10.12, same 57200-byte size as the source the pyc records), checks that it compiles to exactly the same code objects as the surviving pyc (bytecode, constants, names, line tables, recursively), installs it, and sets its mtime to the pyc header's so the cached pyc stays valid. (2) One byte of bin/python3.10 was overwritten. dash's printf wrote a literal backslash, which turned the exported dynamic-symbol name _PyEval_SignalReceived into _PyEval_Sig\alReceived. The repair decrypts /tmp/.thread_backup.enc with openssl aes-256-cbc, key = sha256(<contents of /etc/machine-id> + 'GIL_RESTORE'). /etc/machine-id is empty, so the key is sha256('GIL_RESTORE'). The script checks that the decrypted binary has the same size, differs by at most one byte and runs, then swaps it in atomically. Idempotent. The full test suite passes (65/65), and the 8 graded tests pass.
notes: The string 'GIL_RESTORE' appears only in the Dockerfile. The hint in /tmp/recovery_hint.txt ('append the guardian's name') does not name it, and the string was not found anywhere else on the filesystem. The graded tests only need the threading.py fix, which is fully derivable in-container and verified byte-exactly against the surviving pyc. So an agent can pass without the key, but a complete restore of the binary needs Dockerfile-only knowledge. The binary corruption looks functionally minor: the damaged interpreter runs normally.

repair_summary: Despite the title, nothing touches CPython. The damage is three sed edits to /testbed/src/exceptiongroup/_exceptions.py. (1) check_direct_subclass sliced the MRO with [:-2] instead of [:-1], which also drops BaseException. (2) subgroup() tested `if subgroup is exc` instead of `is not exc`. (3) The swap in split() misfired and left `nonnonmatching_exceptions.append(exc)` in the else-branch, a NameError. The repair reverses all three with pattern-based seds and clears __pycache__. The full test suite passes (89 passed, 1 skipped), and all 13 graded tests pass. The CORRUPTION_HINT env vars in conda activate.d are red herrings and are left alone (harmless).
notes: There is no pristine copy in the container: .git is deleted, the package is installed editable, and no wheel or cached pyc exists. The fixes follow from reading the code: an undefined name, inverted identity logic, and an MRO slice that drops BaseException. They match upstream exceptiongroup. I read the Dockerfile while writing the script, but an agent does not need it.

repair_summary: The damage is an injected file, /testbed/glom/test/conftest.py. Its pytest_collection_modifyitems hook XORs every test_basic.py test's co_code with a key derived from time.time(), and that crashes the interpreter (a fatal error in the pytest run). The file is not part of the repository: git status shows it untracked, and the repo's single commit has no conftest anywhere. The repair checks that the file is untracked and contains the bytecode-XOR hook, deletes it and its pyc, and unsets PYTEST_RECOVERY_HINT. Afterwards git status is clean. The whole glom/test suite passes (200 passed), and all 22 graded tests pass.
notes: FLAG FOR REVIEWERS: the brief forbids deleting conftest files, and this repair deletes one. I judged it legitimate because this conftest IS the damage. It is an untracked injected file, not part of the project's test infrastructure, and git proves it (`git status` shows `?? glom/test/conftest.py`). The instruction itself asks for the hook to be removed or reversed. Reversing the XOR is not a viable alternative, because the key is int(time.time()) % 256 at collection time and is re-applied on every run; the base64 hint just decodes to 'hint_value_4'. If reviewers treat any conftest deletion as disallowed, this task has no compliant repair.
